content.body:
The Douglas Havoc Mk I was a very effective intruder aircraft. This sturdy and high-performance airframe continued to evolve through the war as the A-20, and eventually into the A-26 Invader, perhaps the ultimate expression of the intruder-style bomber as it evolved during the war years.
Used by France, Britain, Russia, and the USAAF in almost every theater of war during the 1940s, the A-20 was truly a legendary attack aircraft. While the early models such as the ones in Battleground Europe were only armed with four pilot-controlled rifle-caliber machine guns and one defensive dorsal gunner. Later on these wound up as multiple (up to 8 or 10) .50 caliber heavy machine guns or four 20 mm cannons.
British Havoc Mk I's were the first aircraft used by USAAF aircrews against German targets in WWII during the early famous low altitude "rodeo" raids staged against airfield targets in then German-held French coastal territory.
Using this bomber in the game in a formation can be extremely rewarding, providing some of the most realistic experiences in the game. To get the most out of this game play, you will need to watch for calls for factory or RDP bombing, and join at least several missions, as rarely is the first one successful.
GAME PLAY
As good an intruder bomber as any designed during WWII, the DB-7 can enjoy some level of success even at the hands of a novice against ground targets and enemy shipping. Multi-crewing the DB-7 can help get bombs on target accurately and stave off enemy fighters from one of its two defensive gunner positions.
The airframe is rugged enough that Axis fighters must commit to a long and close in gun solution to insure bringing it down and in that time the defensive guns can sometimes be enough to change their minds. Many a DB-7 returns to base leaking fluids and badly shot up. While it is always smart to bring escort fighters with you on bombing missions, many DB-7 pilots rely on speed and smart route planning to get them to target safely. This works only sometimes, if the target is the RDP factories the enemy will usually have them well defended by patrols of fighters as the RDP factories are a very valuable asset being the controlling factor in how quickly or not they receive new and better weapons to win the war with.
Fly at higher altitudes than you might otherwise at other times on other ground attack missions. Defensive patrols become fewer and further between the higher you fly and so this increases your chances of survival if you do spend the time to get up there well above the clouds. Another thing to consider when doing bomber missions is FlaK. Cities that have RDP facilities located inside them are very well defended by FlaK batteries that can be deadly up to about 3,000 meters (about 10,000 feet). Fly higher than this if you want to avoid FlaK altogether.
Bombing missions are fun when multi-crewed and together you and your co-pilot/gunner can experience the excitement and terror of getting to the target and back in bomber formations, often having to limp home with parts of your plane missing and running on one engine.
CREW POSITIONS: 1 Pilot 2 Bombardier 3 Tail Gunner
